interactions.summary: A student reads Beatrice's logic that Adam's disobedience damns his descendants, that humanity falls into a long error, and that the Word descends to reunite severed human nature with God.
Jiang translates the line about just vengeance and just punishment into the basic scandal of Christianity: why an innocent Jesus has to appease God's anger at all.
Jiang glosses the unnamed first sinner in Beatrice's argument as Adam and keeps the reading moving.
Jiang interprets the separation from God as a schism produced by free will: humans are born with a spark of God, turn toward evil, and then compound that estrangement like a snowball.

claims.claim: Jiang says the Christian puzzle is that God's anger at humanity after the Fall is understandable, but it still makes no intuitive sense that an innocent Jesus must sacrifice himself to answer that anger.
The Dante passage Jiang is teaching says Adam's failure to keep the curb on his will damns all his progeny and leaves mankind sick in error for centuries.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted salvific history read and glossed on 2026-06-16.

claims.claim: Jiang says the Fall creates a schism between God and humanity, and Jesus is the descent that reconciles a nature separated from its maker.
Jiang says humans are born good because God's spark of life is in them, but free will lets them choose evil and then spiral farther away through compounding mistakes.
Jiang says once people begin choosing evil, the resulting moral decline behaves like a snowball: one bad act leads to another until the right path is hard to recover.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang makes the atonement problem feel scandalous rather than routine by asking why an innocent man must pay to calm God's anger.
signature_moments.source_phrase: why should this man who's innocent jesus have to sacrifice himself in order to appease god's anger at us
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It prevents the packet from dissolving into doctrine and keeps the emotional force of the question alive.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang compresses the Fall into a schism: humans and God are separated and do not even know how to ask forgiveness.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we don't even know how to ask forgiveness
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This sharpens the need for mediation instead of leaving sin as a vague moral stain.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns sin into an accumulating downhill motion rather than a single isolated act.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The snowball image gives the packet a memorable model for why fallen will cannot simply self-correct.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The first sinner whose misuse of will in Beatrice's argument becomes the origin of the human fall and inherited estrangement.
Jiang's word for the separation between God and humanity after the Fall, which redemption must somehow heal.
Jiang's shorthand for the divine essence breathed into humans at creation, used to explain why human beings begin good.

chronology_notes.note: This 2026-06-16 packet moves from Adam's original disobedience through centuries of fallen human history into Jiang's present-tense model of compounding evil and lost moral direction.

uncertainty_notes.note: The ASR is rough in places around Jiang's improvised explanation, but the core structure is clear: humans contain a divine spark, misuse free will, and then drift farther through accumulating evil.
